BiblicalUsage: Asenath is the daughter of Potipherah, priest of On, whom Pharaoh gives to Joseph as wife. She bears him Manasseh and Ephraim 'before the years of famine came', and her sons are named in the genealogy of the tribes when Jacob's family goes down into Egypt.
TheologicalSignificance: An Egyptian priest's daughter becomes the mother of two tribes of Israel — and the Bible tells it without apology. I believe Asenath is a reminder that God's family grows in surprising ways: the sons of Joseph and an Egyptian woman stand in the inheritance, and grace does not check a birth certificate.
